title: How the Sun's heat crosses empty space
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: How does the Sun's heat reach Earth?
Why do dark clothes get hot in the sun?

figure.name: x-wave
figure.note: Infrared and visible light carry the Sun's energy across space

explain.say: Space between the Sun and Earth is almost empty, so there is no air to carry heat by conduction or convection. The Sun's heat comes to us as radiation.

draw.text: How the Sun's heat crosses empty space

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: Infrared and visible light carry the Sun's energy across space

explain.say: The Sun sends out light waves of many wavelengths. Some we see, and some, called infrared, are invisible but carry lots of heat. They cross space at the speed of light.

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: Infrared has longer waves than red light

explain.say: When the rays hit something, it absorbs some of their energy and warms up. That is why sunshine feels warm on your skin even on a cold winter day.

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: Infrared and visible light carry the Sun's energy across space

explain.say: Dark, dull surfaces absorb most of the radiation and heat up fast, while white or shiny surfaces reflect it and stay cooler. That is why dark clothes feel hotter in the sun.

faq.q: How does heat get from the Sun to Earth?
faq.a: By radiation. The Sun gives out light and infrared waves that travel through empty space, and when they land on Earth they are absorbed and turn into heat.
asks: How does sunlight warm the Earth?

faq.a: Infrared is a kind of light with waves a little longer than red light, so our eyes cannot see it. We feel it as heat, and warm things give it out.

faq.q: Why do dark things get hotter in sunshine?
faq.a: Dark surfaces absorb most of the light that hits them and turn it into heat. Light and shiny surfaces reflect most of it away, so they stay cooler.
asks: Why do black cars get so hot?

faq.q: Why do you feel warm in sunshine on a cold day?
faq.a: The rays warm your skin directly, even when the air around you is cold, because radiation does not need to heat the air first.
asks: Why is the sun warm in winter?

faq.q: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
faq.a: About 8 minutes and 20 seconds. Light travels around 300,000 kilometres every second, and the Sun is about 150 million kilometres away.
asks: How fast does the Sun's heat get here?

facts: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to travel the 150 million kilometres to Earth.
Roughly half of the Sun's energy reaching the ground arrives as invisible infrared.

quiz.say: Why can't conduction or convection bring the Sun's heat to Earth?
quiz.show: Why can't conduction or convection bring the Sun's heat to Earth?

options.show: Space is almost empty, with no particles to carry it
options.say: Space is almost empty, with no particles to carry it

options.show: The Sun is too far away for light
options.say: The Sun is too far away for light

options.show: Space is too cold for heat
options.say: Space is too cold for heat

quiz.why: Conduction and convection need particles; radiation can cross the near-empty space between the Sun and Earth.

wrong.1: Light does reach us, in about 8 minutes, and it carries the heat.
wrong.2: Radiation crosses cold space without losing its energy to it.
